trigger: A Lua integration design changes host ownership, VM lifecycle, error handling, execution model, performance partition, or type discipline.
steps: Require independent VM states for declared isolation boundaries and explicit create-run-close ownership.
Require script errors to terminate at a protected host catch boundary with host-owned rollback and cleanup.
Keep interpreter-first semantics; treat JIT as optional and separately gated.
Require dynamic boundary checks plus documented internal type discipline.
Record any unpinned Lua implementation/version or undefined resource limit as a runtime blocker, not a reason to weaken the contract.
failureHandling: Reject designs where Lua owns the application loop, cleanup is script-owned, state isolation is shared by default, or JIT is assumed as a prerequisite.
